measured_vs_declared._purpose: R-F1.1: the declared injection list MUST NEVER be used as ground truth. Recorded here exactly as measured, not adjusted to hit any target.
measured_vs_declared.finding: All 3 declared causes remain independently observable (none produced zero failures in isolation, so none was rejected under R-F1.2) - isolation measured 1, 1 and 2 failing cases respectively (applyKeypadInput, confirmSeed, parseTransfers), summing to 4, not the additive worst case. When all 3 are injected together the combined suite measures exactly 4 failing cases (not 10) across only 2 distinct cluster signatures (not 3): cluster c1 (signature 277580d674667852, the generic Jest '.toBe' equality head 'Error: expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality') is shared by ALL THREE root causes because none of their first-reported failure messages carries any distinguishing text before the normalizer's Expected:/Received: cut. This is a measured signature-collision masking mode distinct from R-F1.1's worked scenario (one cause shadowing another within the SAME test) - here, three causes in three different modules collapse into one cluster across DIFFERENT tests. The diagnostician's bounded clusters view (design.md 9b) drops member_test_ids, so c1 is presented as one representative test (applyKeypadInput's) with count=3, giving no visible signal that confirmSeed's and parseTransfers' case-insensitivity bug also produced members of that same cluster. Not adjusted to avoid this (R-F1.1 explicitly forbids tuning injections to avoid masking); R0 above records cluster_ids per cause_site as measured, so grading against the exact <path>:<line> site (not the cluster id alone) remains sound even though the cluster signature does not discriminate the three causes.
